title: Cabinets and junction boxes: where they are and what they hold
summary: A cabinet or junction box is two objects: its location in Areas and the enclosure in Assets. The enclosure holds rails, terminal strips, I/O cards with their channels, interposing devices, power supplies and earth bars.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit objects

title: Add terminals to a strip
summary: Add numbered terminals to a terminal strip, a channel, an earth bar, a power supply or an instrument in one step, counting on from the last one.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit objects

title: Cables, their cores, and landing a core on a terminal
summary: A cable made from a cable type in the catalog gets its cores at once (pairs with their screens, the overall screen). Each core is landed on a terminal at each end.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit objects

title: Trace a circuit
summary: Follow a circuit from an instrument through its cable, the junction box, the multicore and the marshalling to the I/O channel, with every terminal's reference designation.
roles: Anyone who may view the project

title: Construction status of cores and terminals
summary: Mark cores, cables and terminals as issued for construction, installed, terminated, loop-checked or as-built.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit relationships

title: Cable lengths and the wiring settings
summary: A cable has a length by hand and a length from 3D; E1 uses the one by hand and reports when they differ by more than the project's tolerance. Project settings → Wiring holds the tolerance and which names documents print first.
roles: A project role that may configure the project (settings); a license and a project role that may edit objects (lengths)

title: Import existing or vendor wiring
summary: A termination list of an existing plant or a vendor's panel is imported with a preview: the enclosures, strips, terminals, cables and cores not yet in the project are made, and every core is landed as fixed, with its scope and construction status.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit objects

title: Loop diagrams from the wiring
summary: The loop diagram follows each circuit of a loop through the junction boxes, cables, marshalling and barriers to the I/O channel, with its power feed and its screen, in columns by zone; the loop diagrams of a unit are generated and issued as one set.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit documents

title: Wire list, termination list, cable schedule and I/O list
summary: Each of these lists is a query you build and save once: E1 ships none (examples below). They read the same wiring as the loop diagram, so they never go stale.
roles: Anyone who may view the project; saving for the project needs a role that may edit it

title: Signals and wiring typicals
summary: Give devices their signals and a wiring typical with options and variants; E1 names wires, terminals and cables from it.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit objects

title: Allocation and Panorama EI&C
summary: E1 proposes where every signal lands by the segregation rules and spares; you walk it hop by hop in Panorama EI&C and accept it.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit relationships
